name: Jeff Cardenas
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Apptronik (Austin, TX humanoid robotics)
profile: UT Austin BBA '08 / MSTC '13 who co-founded Apptronik in 2016 as a spin-out of UT's Human Centered Robotics Lab with Luis Sentis, Nick Paine and Bill Helmsing. Apptronik builds the Apollo humanoid, partners with Google DeepMind, and closed a $935M+ Series A in Feb 2026 (valued ~$5B).
interesting_fact: When Apptronik started, he says, 'everyone told us not to do humanoids'; he framed humanoids as a 'PC moment for robotics' and Apptronik later partnered with Google DeepMind on AI-powered humanoids.
deep_cut_fact: Son of an Air Force colonel, he grew up playing with Transformers; after his BBA he first tried a mobile-app startup (market was oversaturated), then spent four years at Deloitte and worked at UT's IC2 Institute, where he met mentor Gen. Bill Welch and the robotics team.
notes: Frequent podcast/conference guest (TechFirst, Automated podcast, SiliconANGLE theCUBE) - receptive to media. Head of Communications Liz Clinkenbeard is the named media contact on press releases.

name: Zhang Di
current_role: Unclear; formerly chairman of ExPace (CASIC rocket subsidiary, now Kuaizhou Aerospace) and VP of CASIC Fourth Academy
profile: The listing ('CASIC founder; $2B') most plausibly refers to Zhang Di (张镝), founding chairman of ExPace/CASIC Rocket Technology Co., the state-linked maker of Kuaizhou solid rockets, while also VP of CASIC's Fourth Academy. ExPace (renamed Kuaizhou Aerospace in July 2026) is now chaired by Zha Xiongquan. Could not confirm current role.
interesting_fact: After the Jan 2017 Kuaizhou-1A launch he touted the rocket's cost at around $10,000 per kg of payload, 'extremely competitive'.
notes: CASIC is a state-owned defense conglomerate, not a founder-led startup; Hurun 'founder' label is doubtful. Executive of a Chinese SOE defense group - very unlikely podcast guest; no published personal contacts.

name: David Gunn
current_role: Co-founder, Vantaca (one company profile lists him as Co-founder & CIO; not on current leadership page)
profile: Software developer who co-founded Vantaca in Wilmington, NC in 2015 with HOA-management operator Dave Sweyer, building a platform first for Sweyer's management firm CAMS. Vantaca bootstrapped to scale, then took JMI Equity and Cove Hill investment; it now serves 500+ community-management companies (~$1B+ valuation). CEO is Ben Currin.
interesting_fact: Vantaca's own site credits it as founded in 2015 by Dave Sweyer and David Gunn on the belief that community management companies 'deserved software that actually worked for how they run their business.'
notes: Very low public profile; almost no press about him personally. Many unrelated David Gunns online - be careful. Best route is via Vantaca general contact or CEO Ben Currin.

name: Rob Slaughter
profile: Former Air Force major (13 years) with a PhD in engineering physics from AFIT who led the DoD's Platform One and helped launch Kessel Run and SpaceCAMP. Left in 2021 to co-found Defense Unicorns with Jeff McCoy and Andrew Greene; its open-source Unified Defense Stack runs in 150+ military systems and a $136M Series B (Jan 2026, Bain Capital) valued it above $1B.
interesting_fact: Defense Unicorns was bootstrapped on a $500K family investment, consulting work and small grants, and was profitable most years before raising venture money; ~40% of staff are veterans and he does the final interview for every hire.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Phoenix as the son of postal workers; unable to afford tuition, he joined Air Force ROTC to study physics, inspired by a grandfather who was an Air Force veteran and later a Lockheed Martin contractor.

public_contacts.value: Defense Unicorns, A Podcast (co-hosted by Robert Slaughter)

notes: Media email is from an Oct 2024 release; confirm still active. Hosts his own podcast, so likely open to podcast appearances.
